candidates.name: cand_pattern_table
candidates.hypothesis: Linguini problems (language pattern learning) currently succeed at 25% with informal pattern matching. By asking the model to build explicit morphological component tables, verify them against all examples, and apply rules systematically (rather than reasoning informally), we create better scaffolding for pattern discovery. Unlike cand_decomposed_subgoals which forced structure everywhere, this only activates for language/morphology problems, preserving performance on other problem types.

candidates.name: cand_selective_code
candidates.hypothesis: cand_code_solver failed (29.2%) because it applied code generation to logic puzzles and boolean expressions where it was inappropriate. By being much more selective—only triggering code for state-tracking problems with explicit initial state, swap operations, and domain context (dance/gift/partner)—we can help shuffled_objects problems while preserving baseline performance on logical reasoning problems.
